//: The ACG groups the original Open webOS apps get on a Phoenix image. They predate webOS OSE's access
control groups and declare no requiredPermissions; without groups luna-hub refuses their calls.
tools/install-rootfs.py writes these into each app's client permissions
(/usr/share/luna-service2/client-permissions.d/<id>.app.json, as meta-webos's
webos_app_generate_security_files does from requiredPermissions); tools/check-luna.py checks the calls
against them. The lists start from `tools/check-luna.py --suggest` (the groups OSE's api files give the
methods each app calls directly), plus database.operation and activity.operation for the apps that keep
their data in db8 and schedule activities through the frameworks (DbService, foundations' Mojo.Service),
which the checker charges to the frameworks, not the app; and phoenix.appmanager.query for the apps that load
Enyo's accounts library (depends.js), whose account templates with a customUI open in Enyo's CrossAppUI
(com.palm.applicationManager/getAppBasePath; enyo-1.0 framework/source/palm/system/CrossAppUI.js:19).
Accounts also holds the connectors' sign-in groups: a template's customUI page is a frame of Accounts' card,
and WebAppMgr's bridge gives the frame's calls Accounts' name (docs/DEVICE-AUDIT.md, "Accounts and their
connectors on Revision 22"; tools/check-luna.py charges each page to Accounts). Each group has only the
methods its page calls (the owner's decision, 27 November 2026: least privilege, not the connectors' whole
account groups): phoenix.dav.validate (DAV's and the subscribed calendar's pages), phoenix.fediverse.signin,
phoenix.telegram.signin, phoenix.drives.signin (the drives' fields, OAuth, Nextcloud Login Flow and SFTP
keys), and phoenix.appmanager.open for the pages' sign-up links (com.palm.applicationManager/open alone).
The same for Phoenix's own catalog connectors (preinstalled.json firstParty), each its page's methods only:
phoenix.<bluesky|google|linkedin|microsoft|slack|todoist|zoom>.signin (ConnectorWizard.js: providerInfo,
checkCredentials, signIn), phoenix.matrix.signin (signInOptions, checkCredentials, signIn), phoenix.xmpp.signin
(checkCredentials), phoenix.deltachat.signin (available, checkCredentials). Interim: any page in Accounts' frame
holds all of these, so the catalogs refuse a third-party connector's own sign-in page (connector rule C17) until
each page runs as its own connector (docs/ROADMAP.md, per-connector sign-in isolation).
The same rule on the device: before it frames a template's own sign-in page, the accounts library (compat overlay
lib/accounts/source/cross-app.js) asks the Marketplace's service whether the page is Phoenix's own
(org.webosphoenix.service.packages/checkSignInPage alone: phoenix.packages.signin), for every app that loads
the library and frames such pages (the holders of phoenix.appmanager.query above: Accounts, Calendar, Email).
